elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 6.1 reads: "The Company shall have no restriction under this Agreement on the products it may offer or the projects or web sites in which it may participate, and HDI shall have no exclusive right to use of the 'Deerskin' brand." The original prohibition on participating in any project similar to the Site with respect to Deerskin Products or "products substantially similar" (including "companies similar to" named competitors) is gone, and the Vendor-side exclusive right over Customer's own "Deerskin" brand — which would otherwise have prevented Customer from using its own brand and left a field-of-use restriction in substance — is also removed. Section 6.3 restricts HDI only, which is acceptable.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no restriction on Customer survives in Section 6.1 or elsewhere in the cited text, so there is no scope that could exceed a single named competing product.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with the covenant deleted, no obligation runs during or after the term. The auto-renewal mechanic in Section 4.1 is untouched but no longer carries any restrictive covenant.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no surviving duration because the covenant itself has been removed.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the affirmative language confirms Customer has "no restriction ... on the products it may offer or the projects or web sites in which it may participate," so internal development is unimpeded and no carve-out is required.
Condition does not apply: no covenant remains that could reach acquired businesses or products.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the Customer-side covenant and the Vendor exclusive right over Customer's own brand are both removed, so no non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds Customer. Per the rule boundary, deleting only the covenant while leaving HDI's exclusive "Deerskin" brand right would have left the result incomplete; the drafter correctly removed both.
Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because no restriction survives; nothing exceeds the named-product, in-term, 12-month, internal-development or acquisition limits.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to Section 6.1. Section 6.2 (a Customer-favourable retained right) and Section 6.3 (Vendor-side restriction, which the playbook says is fine) are untouched, and Section 4.1 is quoted only as context and left unchanged. The short affirmative replacement sentence is a permissible rendering of the deletion — it adds no obligation, survival tail, expense allocation, remedy or procedure outside the checklist, and it avoids the dangling "Except as provided in Section 6.2" opener that a bare strike-through would have left.

Intent is preserved: the closeout-merchandise right in 6.2 stands on its own without the now-removed cross-reference, the term/termination mechanics and the balance of the hosting arrangement are unaffected, and no defined term (Deerskin Products, Termination Date) is orphaned or contradicted by the new sentence.

Note for the drafter: confirm no other section (e.g. any operational or supply provision outside the cited text) independently obliges the Company to route Deerskin Products exclusively through the Site, since the new blanket "no restriction under this Agreement" wording would otherwise sit in tension with such a clause; if one exists, conform it rather than relying on the 6.1 override.
